pr_title: boards: nucleo_f103rb: Prevent Wundef on build
pr_body:
As described in issue [28854](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/28854), there are configuration options which might not be defined, and will cause `Wundef` warnings (and subsequently errors with `Werror`) when building on a nucleo-f103rb board.

Fixes #28854.
pr_comments: Closing, I unfortunately haven't had time to expand this fix more broadly and will not in the immediate future.

issue_context.title: `CONFIG_STACK_POINTER_RANDOM` may be undefined
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

In some builds, it may be possible for `CONFIG_STACK_POINTER_RANDOM` to be undefined. This will trigger a warning (leading to an error if `Werror` is present) in GCC when `Wundef` is set.

**To Reproduce**

Seen using PlatformIO, have no reason to believe that this is related to the PIO code, however.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Prepare the the 'blinky' sample project for [Nucleo-F103RB](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/1.14.1/samples/basic/blinky/README.html#blinky-sample). 

2. Add following build flags:
```
    -Werror
    -Wall
    -Wextra
    -Warray-bounds
    -Wno-sign-conversion  # Zephyr
    -Wlogical-op
    -Wformat-overflow
    -Wformat=2
    # -Wshadow  # Zephyr
    -Wstringop-overflow
    -Wswitch-default
    -Wundef
    -Wno-unknown-pragmas
    -fstack-protector-strong
```
3. Attempt to build image using preferred toolchain (reproduced using PlatformIO build, should be reproducible using ninja/west as well)

**Expected behavior**
No warnings in the Zephyr kernel code due to `Wundef`

Observe warnings similar to the following:
```
/home/j/.platformio/packages/framework-zephyr/kernel/include/kernel_internal.h:122:5: error: "CONFIG_STACK_POINTER_RANDOM" is not defined, evaluates to 0 [-Werror=undef]
```

**Impact**

Need to disable warnings that would normally be enabled as blocking failures in our codebase, or explicitly exclude Zephyr files from analysis.

comments: We probably should not be using `#if` here and instead use #if defined()

I'm happy to push a trivial PR with something like:

```
#if defined(CONFIG_STACK_POINTER_RANDOM)
```

or

```
#if defined(CONFIG_STACK_POINTER_RANDOM) && CONFIG_STACK_POINTER_RANDOM == 1
```

if preferred.

review_comments:
There are more than 250 occurrences in current master of 
`#if DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS(DT_NODELABEL(foox), okay) && defined(CONFIG_FOO)`

Some of them (which current occurrence is part of), will disappear as part of #28999.
But I think this should be addressed globally anyway.

@erwango I agree, per this commit message:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/29208/commits/a4befb2c6c7ea1bd9bf6ec5c12fb4bc02cc7ea49

"Prevent `Wundef` warnings from occurring due to missing CONFIG_ symbols.
Note that the pattern fixed here is pervasive across other files in the
`boards/` directory, and it may be worth applying the same changes
to all other cases found with `ack "\) && CONFIG"`."

Unfortunately, I have no time to spend on this effort in the next 1-2 weeks, but feel free to contribute a more global solution if you wish (I am happy to pick it back up later this month if still relevant, however, and would be curious to know the approach/pattern you'd suggest for CI in this case - adding a custom linter rule?).

Stepping back another level, theres also the question of `#ifdef` vs `#if defined(`, but I'm assuming we are not looking to resolve that style difference across the project right now.
